newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire will be at next HK land auction.
newsitem.headline: Swire will be at next HK land auction.

text.p: Hong Kong conglomerate Swire Pacific Ltd said on Saturday it would be present at the next Hong Kong government land auction on Tuesday when two major residential sites will be put up for sale.
"We will be at the auction on Tuesday," chairman Peter Sutch told reporters.

The two sites, a 571,848 square-foot plot in beachside Stanley on Hong Kong Island and a 79,675 st ft waterfront site in Kowloon's Hunghom, are expected to draw keen interest from Hong Kong's major property developers.

Sutch said Swire would continue to take a cautious approach to land bank acquisitions in the future but hoped that a recent purchase of a site in Hong Kong's Tseung Kwan O had put to rest investor concerns that the company's land bank was dwindling.
Swire Properties Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd's New Town Properties Ltd acquired the right to develop the Shui Wing Steel mill site in Tseung Kwan O in April.

"I hope that we have put to bed the sort of belief that was beginning to sort of take hold that not only was our land bank down the track beginning to dwindle but that we were not interested in replenishing it," Sutch said.

"Don't underestimate the land bank we have. 1998 in terms of development profits will be flattish but we do have a number of other sites...and who knows over the next week or so we might have something else," he added.

Sutch said Swire's balance sheet and gearing would allow it to bid for certain big sites alone. "Like the rest of the Hong Kong property development community there are times when we will go it alone and there are times when we will team up," he said.

But he added: "I don't want to give the impression that we are going to buy on Tuesday come hell or high water because we will only pay what we consider to be a price upon which we can get a decent return for the shareholders."

Sutch also said that Swire Pacific was likely to get more active in the Chinese property market in the future but had no specific projects in mind. The company does not currently have a land bank in China. "I think that decision not to leap into that market has proven to be a wise one," he said.
"I believe in the medium term we are likely to be more involved in the China property market."
